paragraphs.title: Rejecting Jeremiah’s Message and Accusing Baruch

answers: All the people
The king of Babylon
The captains only
easy.explanation: Jeremiah finished speaking the Lord’s words unto all the people.
easy.q: To whom did Jeremiah finish speaking all the words of the Lord?

answers: Baruch and Nebuzaradan
Azariah, Johanan, and all the proud men
The kings of Egypt and Babylon
easy.explanation: Azariah, Johanan, and the proud men accused Jeremiah of speaking falsely.
easy.q: Who said to Jeremiah, “Thou speakest falsely”?

answers: Nebuchadrezzar
Gedaliah
Baruch the son of Neriah
easy.explanation: They said that Baruch was setting Jeremiah on against them.
easy.q: Whom did they accuse of setting Jeremiah on against them?

answers: The Lord had not sent Jeremiah to tell them not to go into Egypt
The Lord had sent Jeremiah to lead them to Babylon
The Lord had sent Jeremiah to appoint a new king
medium.explanation: They claimed that the Lord had not sent Jeremiah to say, “Go not into Egypt.”
medium.q: What did the men claim about the Lord’s command concerning Egypt?

answers: Save them from the Egyptians
Deliver them to the Chaldeans and cause them to be carried away to Babylon
Return them to the land of Judah
medium.explanation: They accused Baruch of trying to deliver them into the hand of the Chaldeans.
medium.q: What did the proud men claim Baruch wanted to do to them?

answers: They accepted the message but feared obeying it
They rejected Jeremiah’s message and authority
They did not know who Jeremiah was
medium.explanation: Calling Jeremiah’s words false shows that they rejected both his message and his authority.
medium.q: What does the phrase “Thou speakest falsely” show about their response?

answers: They accepted the prophecy but blamed Baruch for carrying it out
They rejected the prophecy and explained it as Baruch’s plot
They asked Baruch to give them a different prophecy
challenge.explanation: After rejecting Jeremiah’s words, they claimed that Baruch was the person influencing him.
challenge.q: How were the accusations against Baruch connected with the people’s rejection of Jeremiah?

answers: Fear of being delivered to the enemy and carried away captive
Fear of finding no water in the wilderness
Fear of having to serve in Pharaoh’s house
challenge.explanation: They feared being handed over to the Chaldeans, put to death, or carried captive to Babylon.
challenge.q: What fear is expressed in the claim about the Chaldeans and Babylon?

answers: They were ready to obey but needed more information
They were determined to reject the command and follow their own plan
They were confused about whether Egypt was a real place
challenge.explanation: Their accusation was a direct rejection of the Lord’s command delivered through Jeremiah.
challenge.q: What does their accusation suggest about their willingness to obey the Lord?

paragraphs.title: The People Go Down to Egypt Against the Command

answers: The voice of the Lord
The voice of Baruch
The voice of the king of Egypt
easy.explanation: They did not obey the voice of the Lord to dwell in the land of Judah.
easy.q: Whose voice did Johanan, the captains, and the people not obey?

answers: Babylon
Egypt
The land of the Philistines
easy.explanation: They came into the land of Egypt and went as far as Tahpanhes.
easy.q: Where did Johanan and the people go?

answers: Only the army captains
Only the women and children
Men, women, children, the king’s daughters, Jeremiah, and Baruch
easy.explanation: The passage lists these people among those taken to Egypt.
easy.q: Who was taken with the remnant of Judah?

answers: They took the remnant of Judah and led them into Egypt
They sent the people to Babylon
They remained in Judah by themselves
medium.explanation: They took the remnant of Judah, along with Jeremiah and Baruch, into Egypt.
medium.q: What did Johanan and the captains do after refusing to obey the Lord?

answers: The people who remained from Judah
The people who came from Egypt
The army captains only
medium.explanation: The remnant was the group of Judeans who remained after earlier scattering and captivity.
medium.q: In this passage, what does “the remnant of Judah” mean?

answers: Because they obeyed the Lord
Because they obeyed not the voice of the Lord
Because Baruch commanded them
medium.explanation: The text plainly says they came to Egypt because they did not obey the Lord’s voice.
medium.q: Why does the passage say that they came into the land of Egypt?

answers: The people were told to dwell in Judah, but they went to Egypt
The people were told to go to Babylon, but they stayed in Judah
The people were told to fight, but they returned to Jerusalem
challenge.explanation: They refused to remain in Judah and instead went down into Egypt.
challenge.q: What is the main contrast in these verses?

answers: They freely chose to leave Judah
They were taken along with the remnant of Judah
They were sent ahead to Babylon
challenge.explanation: The passage says that Johanan and the captains took Jeremiah and Baruch with them.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from Jeremiah and Baruch being taken with the travelers?

answers: They arrived in Egypt, then refused to stay in Judah, and afterward were taken to Egypt
They refused the Lord’s voice, were taken from Judah, and came to Tahpanhes
Jeremiah hid the stones, and then the people left Judah
challenge.explanation: The passage presents their disobedience, their removal from Judah, and their arrival at Tahpanhes.
challenge.q: Which order of events is correct?

paragraphs.title: The Stones at Tahpanhes as a Sign of Nebuchadnezzar’s Arrival

answers: Tahpanhes
Babylon
The land of Judah
easy.explanation: The word of the Lord came unto Jeremiah in Tahpanhes.
easy.q: Where was Jeremiah when the word of the Lord came unto him?

answers: A great sword
Great stones
A scroll
easy.explanation: The Lord commanded Jeremiah to take great stones in his hand.
easy.q: What did the Lord command Jeremiah to take in his hand?

answers: In the wilderness
In Jeremiah’s house
In the clay in the brickkiln at the entry of Pharaoh’s house
easy.explanation: He was to hide them in the clay in the brickkiln at Pharaoh’s house in Tahpanhes.
easy.q: Where was Jeremiah to hide the stones?

answers: In the sight of the men of Judah
In the sight of the Chaldeans only
In the sight of the king of Judah only
medium.explanation: The stones were to be hidden in the sight of the men of Judah.
medium.q: In whose sight was Jeremiah to perform this act?

answers: A place or structure associated with making bricks
The palace of the king of Babylon
A gate in a city of Judah
medium.explanation: The brickkiln was the place near Pharaoh’s house where Jeremiah hid the stones in clay.
medium.q: What is the brickkiln in this passage?

answers: The immediate return of the Jews to Judah
The coming of Nebuchadrezzar and the setting of his throne above them
The building of a new temple
medium.explanation: The Lord said that Nebuchadrezzar would set his throne upon the hidden stones.

answers: They were to witness the prophetic sign
They were to learn how to make bricks
They were to carry the stones to Egypt
challenge.explanation: Their presence made them witnesses of the sign Jeremiah performed.
challenge.q: Why is it important that the act was performed in the sight of the men of Judah?

answers: A place in Egypt became the sign of Babylon’s coming rule
The place represented the people’s return to Judah
The place was meant to hide the Lord’s word from the Jews
challenge.explanation: Although the people had gone to Egypt, that location would mark Nebuchadrezzar’s arrival.
challenge.q: How does the location of the stones relate to the prophetic message?

answers: They would take the people to Egypt
Nebuchadrezzar’s throne would be set upon them
They were given to Baruch
challenge.explanation: The throne placed upon the stones gives them a symbolic and prophetic meaning.
challenge.q: Which detail shows that the stones were more than building material?

paragraphs.title: The Calamity That Will Come Upon Egypt

answers: Nebuchadrezzar
Baruch
Johanan
easy.explanation: Nebuchadrezzar, king of Babylon, would smite the land of Egypt.
easy.q: Who would smite the land of Egypt?

answers: Death, captivity, and the sword
Peace, prosperity, and rebuilding
Exile, famine, and pestilence only
easy.explanation: The passage speaks of those appointed to death, captivity, and the sword.
easy.q: What fates are mentioned for the people in Egypt?

answers: They would be rebuilt
They would be burned with fire
They would become palaces of Judah
easy.explanation: The Lord said that fire would be kindled in the houses of Egypt’s gods.
easy.q: What would happen to the houses of the gods of Egypt?

answers: He would take it away
He would return it to Judah
He would hide it in Pharaoh’s house
medium.explanation: The passage says that Nebuchadrezzar would carry away Egypt’s goods and people.
medium.q: What would Nebuchadrezzar do with the wealth of Egypt?

answers: Those destined for captivity would be taken captive
Those destined for death would be rescued
Those destined for the sword would return to Judah
medium.explanation: The phrase describes the different fates assigned to the people, including captivity.
medium.q: What does “such as are for captivity to captivity” mean?

answers: Only the houses of Judah
The images of Bethshemesh and the houses of the Egyptian gods
Only Pharaoh’s house
medium.explanation: The passage mentions the breaking of Bethshemesh’s images and the burning of the Egyptian gods’ houses.
medium.q: Which places or structures would be destroyed?

answers: The calamity would affect everyone in exactly the same way
The people would suffer different fates
Only soldiers would be affected
challenge.explanation: The passage lists several different outcomes for those in Egypt.
challenge.q: What does the division among death, captivity, and the sword show?

answers: Both are acts of destroying Egyptian places or objects of worship
Both are acts of rebuilding
The first happens in Judah and the second in Babylon
challenge.explanation: Both actions represent the destruction of Egyptian religious structures and images.
challenge.q: What is the connection between burning the houses of the gods and breaking the images of Bethshemesh?

answers: The conqueror will take Egypt as easily as a shepherd puts on a garment and then depart in peace
The shepherd will lead Israel through the wilderness
The Egyptians will receive new clothing
challenge.explanation: The image presents Nebuchadrezzar as taking possession of Egypt and then going forth from it in peace.
challenge.q: What does the shepherd comparison suggest when Nebuchadrezzar arrays himself with the land of Egypt?
